inv_resolves_to: /opt/investigation/bin/inv
Preserve evidence, test explanations, and evaluate options.
Usage: inv [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
Commands:
init           Create a local workspace and an optional Markdown vault
demo           Generate a reproducible tutorial workspace from a worked scenario
record         Submit one atomic transaction using the operation catalog
ingest         Preserve original local bytes and return their acquisition IDs
start          Open an exploratory case and retain one attachment atomically
evidence       Inspect retained source material explicitly
capture        Record an external producer's run through the inv.capture.v1 protocol
schema         Discover operation schemas, examples, and repairs
onboard        Learn the model and inspect the next valid local action
docs           Print embedded offline docs: the agent instructions or the optional skill
next           Rank up to three snapshot-bound investigative gaps
frontier       List every snapshot-bound gap with filters, paging and rule explanations
blindspots     Audit recorded structure for gaps; never a completeness certificate
guide          Print one method card from the built-in pack or a pinned pack
method         List method packs and their cards
receipt        Look up a command without resubmitting its original input
show           Read a case record at title, summary, or full depth
brief          Read a bounded handoff from the verified case snapshot
explain        Walk the recorded evidence and assessment chain behind one record
review-packet  Read a blinded review packet: question, evidence and criteria, no conclusion
retrospective  Read a case's retrospectives and lessons, its process digest, or admitted lessons
calibration    Brier calibration of resolved likelihoods by self-reported model family
search         Find records by text; results are labelled pointers, not evidence
exposure       Diagnose where exposed text lives in this workspace; removes nothing
retention      Preview withdrawing Artifact availability, or reclaim bytes nothing holds any more
check          Verify the journal, blobs, and index without repairing them
repair         Rebuild derived workspace data or retire settled capture staging
migrate        Dry-run or apply a workspace format migration, with a verified backup first
vault          Publish the working vault and inspect its health and drift
export         Write an immutable report or bundle of one case at one verified snapshot to a new directory
config         Read the effective workspace settings and where each value comes from; never writes
archive        Verify an export offline, or restore or fork a workspace archive; needs no workspace
doctor         Report versions, capabilities, limits, filesystem support and workspace health
integration    Show, apply or remove the agent instructions in a file you name; never implicit
obsidian       Preview or apply a few named native viewer settings in a vault you name
observe        Record one source-bound text observation.
note           Attach one narrative note without evidentiary standing.
case           Create and inspect case-level items.
source         Add source material through verified ingest.
help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
Options:
--workspace <PATH>  Open this workspace instead of discovering the nearest investigation.toml
--case <ID>         Select a case by full ID or unique case_ prefix
--actor <ACTOR>     Attribute actions to this actor, or use workspace settings or AGENT
--session <LABEL>   Self-reported session label for evidence reads and writes, or INVESTIGATION_SESSION
--format <FORMAT>   Select text or a single machine-readable JSON object; pretty prints the text form [possible values: text, json, pretty]
--read-only         Reject commands that write or export; INVESTIGATION_READ_ONLY=1 does the same
--no-color          Accepted for compatibility; output is never colored
--no-pager          Accepted for compatibility; output is never paged
-v, --verbose...        Diagnostic logs on stderr: -v info, -vv debug, -vvv trace. INVESTIGATION_LOG sets a level
-q, --quiet             Only log errors on stderr
-h, --help              Print help
-V, --version           Print version
Use investigation when a question needs multiple observations, a comparison, or a handoff.
The workspace preserves evidence and attributed revisions. Writes return a durable receipt.
Examples:
Start a case from a local file in the working directory:
investigation init ./casework --actor agent:investigator --no-vault --import-root . --format json
investigation --workspace ./casework --actor agent:investigator start 'Why did requests time out?' --attach ./results.log --format json
On this machine, later writes that omit --actor are attributed to the actor init --actor recorded.
Continue, record and hand off:
investigation onboard --format json
investigation docs agents
investigation --workspace ./casework brief --format json
investigation --workspace ./casework next --format json
investigation --workspace ./casework case new 'Request latency' --format json
investigation --workspace ./casework source add ./results.log --case <ID> --format json
investigation schema case.create --format json
investigation --workspace ./casework observe 'The log reports 28 seconds' --source <ARTIFACT_ID> --quote 'waited 28 seconds' --format json
investigation --workspace ./casework note 'Check the clock source' --on <RECORD_ID> --format json
investigation --workspace ./casework record --input case.json --format json
investigation --workspace ./casework receipt KEY --actor ACTOR --format json
To learn on a worked tutorial case with real IDs instead (writes only the new directory):
investigation demo ./demo-case --scenario choice
Use schema record for the transaction envelope and schema --list for operations.
Generated shortcut command IDs appear on stderr before writes; reconcile with receipt KEY.
Use --print-envelope to inspect a shortcut request without writing.
Exit codes: 0 success, 2 invalid input, 3 missing workspace, case or reference, 4 conflict,
5 gate refused, 6 integrity failure, 7 busy, IO or unknown durability. With --format json
the failure names its cause in error.code and its retry in error.repair.
